question: Why is this royal secret knowledge easy for kings to perform?
premises: This knowledge is royal, secret, pure, supreme, directly perceived, righteous, easy to do, and imperishable.
It shines among all knowledges and is called self-knowledge here.
Kings such as Janaka have authority in it.
Its great hiddenness makes it secret.
Heroic kshatriya steadiness makes doing and performing it very easy.
Its brahma-worship action entails no expenditure like other actions through enjoyment.
inference: Therefore kings with heroic steadiness are fit to perform this imperishable royal self-knowledge without expenditure.
uncertainties: Compound segmentation and exact syntactic grouping in the supplied glosses remain uncertain.
plain_english: This royal, secret, pure, supreme knowledge is directly perceived, righteous, easy to do, and imperishable; it shines among all knowledges and is called self-knowledge. Kings such as Janaka have authority in it; because it is greatly hidden it is secret, and because of heroic kshatriya steadiness it is very easy to do and perform; and its brahma-worship action entails no expenditure like other actions through enjoyment.
